introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2026. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.

Question ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub mark in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH paper are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

6. (a) On the outline map of Cameroon provided, **locate** and **name**

(i) **ONE** area of high population density,
(ii) A mountain peak,
(iii) A tourist resort,
(iv) An area where petroleum is mined,
(v) An industrial region.

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2026-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_1.png)

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The answer is a **map**: on the outline map of Cameroon (north at the top, the Atlantic coast in the south-west, Lake Chad in the far north), mark each item with a symbol, write its name and add a key (one mark for each item correctly located and named). Positions:

| Item | Example | Where to place it on the outline map |
|---|---|---|
| (i) High population density | **The West Region (Bamileke highlands, around Bafoussam)**. Others: the area around Douala, around Yaounde, the Mandara Mountains in the Far North | In the west of the country, a little north of the coast and inland of the south-west corner |
| (ii) Mountain peak | **Mount Cameroon** (about 4,000 m, the highest peak in the country, an active volcano). Others: Mount Oku, Mount Manengouba | On the coast at the south-west end of the country, near Limbe and Buea |
| (iii) Tourist resort | **Kribi** (beaches, Lobe Falls) or **Limbe** (black sand beaches, botanic garden) | On the Atlantic coast: Limbe in the west near Mount Cameroon, Kribi further south |
| (iv) Petroleum mined | **The Rio del Rey basin** (offshore, off the south-west coast near the Bakassi peninsula). Another: the offshore fields off Kribi | In the sea or on the coast at the extreme south-west, west of Douala |
| (v) Industrial region | **Douala** (the main industrial city and port), with Edea (aluminium smelter). Another: Yaounde, Limbe (oil refinery) | On the coast, in the south-west of the country, east of Mount Cameroon |

Add a title and a key to the map.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) State four reasons why the forest resources of Cameroon need to be conserved.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any four reasons, one mark each.

1. **Protection of plants and animals (biodiversity):** the forests of Cameroon, such as those of the south and east, shelter a great variety of species, including gorillas, chimpanzees and forest elephants, many of which are rare and endangered.
2. **Protection of the soil and water:** tree roots hold the soil and reduce erosion and floods, and forests protect the sources of streams and rivers.
3. **Climate regulation:** forests give out water vapour that helps rainfall and absorb carbon dioxide, which reduces global warming.
4. **A lasting supply of timber and other products:** wood, fuel wood, food, medicines and fibres can be obtained for future generations, and the timber industry keeps jobs and export earnings.
5. **Tourism and culture:** national parks and forests attract tourists, and forest peoples (such as the Baka) depend on the forest for their way of life.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) Describe **FOUR** different ways the Government is using to improve on the tourist industry.
(ii) Suggest **THREE** ways by which youths in Cameroon can be prevented from leaving the villages to towns.

(8+3=11 marks)

(Total = 20 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Four ways in which the Government is improving the tourist industry (8 marks: each way named and described, 2 marks each).**

1. **Building and improving transport infrastructure:** roads (such as the road to Kribi and the motorways), airports (Douala, Yaounde-Nsimalen, Garoua, Maroua) and the port of Kribi make tourist sites easier to reach.
2. **Creating and protecting parks and reserves:** the State has set up and manages national parks and wildlife reserves (such as Waza, Korup, Boumba-Bek and the Dja reserve) and sites for visitors, and pays rangers to protect wildlife.
3. **Encouraging hotels and tourist services:** the ministry in charge of tourism classifies hotels, gives tax and other incentives to investors, and trains workers in hotel and tourism schools, so the quality of service improves.
4. **Advertising and promoting the country:** it takes part in international tourism fairs, organises festivals and cultural events, publishes brochures and websites, and has simplified entry formalities for visitors (an online visa system).
5. **Other answers:** improving security, restoring monuments and palaces (such as the Foumban and Bafut palaces), and creating regional tourist offices.

**(ii) Three ways to prevent youths from leaving the villages for towns (3 marks, one each).**

1. **Provide social amenities in villages:** electricity, drinking water, schools, health centres and recreation, so that life in the village becomes more attractive.
2. **Create jobs and give help to young farmers:** set up small agro-industries (for processing food crops, palm oil or fish), and give credit, seeds, fertiliser and training to youths in modern farming.
3. **Improve rural roads and markets:** this enables farmers to sell their produce at good prices and earn a good income at home.
4. **Other answers:** vocational training centres in rural areas, easier access to land, rural development projects.
